observations: Photo 0: Rear view of a grey/silver refrigerator with a Hisense energy label on the upper left, exposed compressor and mechanical components at the bottom, barcode stickers, and a warning triangle sticker.
Photo 1: Front view of a grey/silver single-door refrigerator with the Hisense logo on the door and an integrated top handle.
Photo 2: Interior with the door open, showing empty wire and glass shelves, door bins, a temperature control dial, and a small container on a lower shelf.

claims.evidence: Hisense logo visible on the front in photo 1 and on the energy label in photo 0; single door shown in photo 1 and interior in photo 2.
Exterior appears grey/silver in photo 0 and photo 1.
One door visible in photo 1 and photo 2.

risks.risk: Refrigerator does not cool or compressor is faulty
risks.proof: Video of the unit powered on and cooling, with a thermometer inside after running for at least two hours.

risks.risk: Door seal or gasket is torn and not sealing properly
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the closed door gasket or a paper-slip test along the seal.

risks.risk: Power plug or cord is damaged, or voltage rating is unsuitable
risks.proof: Photo of the power plug and the electrical rating label.

risks.risk: Interior has odor, mold, or hidden damage not visible in still photos
risks.proof: Video of the door being opened showing a clean interior with no odor or mold.

proof_requests: Video of the refrigerator powered on and cooling
Close-up of the door seal when closed
Photo of the power plug and rating label
Photo of the top interior freezer section if present
response.reason: The item is clearly a used Hisense single-door refrigerator; brand and type are visible in the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case as non-working pending proof of function.
